name: Unit 11/12 - Galen System Focused Review - Musculoskeletal Student

slides.title: MusculoskeletalDiagnostic Tests
text: Shield client's testes, ovaries or pregnant abdomen
Identifies types of tissues, tumors & vascular abnormalities
No pacemakers, hip prosthesis or vascular clips

slides.title: Soft Tissue Trauma
text: CONTUSION – Soft tissue trauma usually resulting from a blow or blunt force injury such as a fall
SPRAIN – Tearing or stretching of the ligaments caused by a sudden pull
STRAIN – Tearing or stretching of the muscle fibers as a result of suddenly pulling them too far

slides.title: Bursitis & Tendonitis
text: Commonly occur in the shoulder, elbow or knee

slides.title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome
text: Compression of the median nerve at the wrist in the carpal tunnel
Occurs with repetitive hand activities & may also be associated with arthritis, hypothyroidism or pregnancy
Tingling, numbness & pain elicited with percussion of median nerve

slides.title: FRACTURES
text: A break in the continuity of the bone
Occur when a bone is subjected to more stress than it can absorb:

slides.title: Fracture Management
text: Pain is continuous, localized,  & increases in severity until the bone fragments are immobilized
Muscle spasms act as a natural splinting to minimize movement of the bone fragments

slides.title: Reduction of Fractures
text: Performed by manual manipulation or skin/skeletal traction
A cast or splint may be applied
Converts a closed into an open fracture
May use internal or external fixation devices
May also be placed in a cast or traction afterwards

slides.title: Internal Fixation
text: Application of screws, plates, pins, wires or nails to hold bone fragments in alignment
May involve removal of damaged bone & replacement with a prosthesis or bone graft

slides.title: External Fixation
text: An external frame is used with multiple pins applied through the bone
Provides more freedom of movement than traction
Used for open fx with nerve & vascular damage
Pin care must be provided routinely:

slides.title: Cast
text: Made of plaster, thermoplastic or fiberglass material
Incorporates joints above and below the fracture
Plaster casts require 24-48 hours to dry
Use hair dryer on cool setting for itching
Examine skin & cast for pressure areas
Assess skin temperature, & any foul odor or drainage
Instruct client to NOT stick objects inside cast
Elevate and place ice for first 48 hours above heart level

slides.title: Traction
text: The exertion of a pulling force applied in two directions to reduce & immobilize a fracture
Provides proper body alignment & reduces muscle spasms
Ensure that weights hang “FREELY” & do not touch the floor
Do not remove or lift weights without an order
Ensure the knot in the rope does not slip

slides.title: Types of Traction
text: Mechanically applied to bone using pins, wires or tongs
Monitor insertion sites for redness, swelling or drainage
Applied using elastic bandages and/or adhesive

slides.title: Types of Traction
text: Used with either skin or skeletal traction
Used to approximate fractures of femur, tibia or fibula
Produced by counterforce other than client
Maintain 20o angle from thigh to bed
Pin care if used with skeletal

slides.title: Hip Fractures
text: No crossing of legs or bending over at waist
Avoid the use of low chairs or toilets
Do not put on socks/shoes by self

slides.title: Amputation
text: Surgical removal of an extremity or part of an extremity
Free drainage is necessary for healing
Is closed after area is free from infection

slides.title: Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA)
text: Inflammation of connective tissue in the joints (hands & feet)
Fatigue, stiffness, pain, limitation in movement

slides.title: Osteoarthritis (OA)
text: Decreased range of motion of joint
Pain gets worse through out the day

slides.title: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
text: Primarily affects the skin, joints & kidneys

slides.title: NGN NCLEX-RN Practice Question
text: The nurse has taught a client who has sustained a right tibial fracture and had an external fixation device applied 36 hours ago. Which of the following statements by the client would indicate a correct understanding of the teaching? Select all that apply.
“I will use chlorhexidine to clean around the pins.”
“I should limit my daily consumption of foods high in vitamin D.”
“I should expect to see some redness around the external pins.”
“I know that the metal rods help steady my leg fracture as it is healing.”
“I will notify my doctor if I experience increased pressure to the point of pain around my heel.”
